feedback.finish: These are the temperate zones. These areas stretch from the dry zones to the Arctic Circle in the Northern Hemisphere and the Antarctic Circle in the Southern Hemisphere.

atoms.text: Much of Europe, including the UK, is located within the temperate zone.
Here, the climate is characterised by less extreme weather. There is a mixture of dry and wet weather with mild temperatures, which are neither extremely hot nor extremely cold.
Areas in the temperate zone experience four distinct seasons and are characterised by warm summers and cool winters.

atoms.b: Continental climates are similar to ((++temperate terrible)) climates, but they have more extreme temperature variations.
Bodies of ((++water animals)) take longer to heat up or cool down than land, so seas keep the temperatures of nearby landmasses stable.
Continental areas that are ((++far_from close_to)) the sea do not benefit from this, so their temperatures fluctuate more.
This climate type is most commonly found in ((++inland coastal)) areas within the ((++continents planets)) of Europe, Asia and North America.

atoms.text: Due to its vast size and distance from the ocean, large parts of Russia experience a continental climate.
The town of Verkhoyansk in Russia recorded the highest ever temperature north of the Arctic Circle, measuring 38 °C.
